body.heading: A letter at a time
paragraphs: Ghost needs no equipment at all. The first player says a letter. The next adds a letter to the end, and so on around the circle. Every player must have a real word in mind that the growing string of letters could become — but the player who actually completes a word of four letters or more loses the round.

So if the letters stand at G-H-O-S, the next player is in danger: adding T finishes “ghost” and loses. A clever player steers earlier, choosing letters that keep several possible words alive while narrowing everyone else's choices.

body.heading: Bluffing and challenges
paragraphs: The spice of the game is the challenge. If you suspect the player before you had no real word in mind — they were just adding a desperate letter — you may challenge. They must name the word they were aiming at. If they cannot, they lose; if they can, you do.

Traditionally, losing a round earns you a letter of the word GHOST, and collecting all five puts you out — which is how the game got its name. Shorter family versions simply play first to three lost rounds.

body.heading: Try it: a friendly first game
paragraphs: Agree your rules before you start: minimum word length four, no names of people or places, and a dictionary (or a trusted phone) as referee. Beginners do well by keeping a few long, flexible words in reserve — words starting with common pairs like ST, TR and PL.

Watch what happens with the letters Q and U, or an awkward K near the end of a string. Ghost rewards players who think two moves ahead, which is exactly what makes it a quiet little strategy game in disguise.

takeaway: In Ghost, the letters are a cliff edge: every player must walk towards a word without being the one who arrives.
